source_title: Vaugondy/Robert 1756, Upper Saxon Circle (southern part) — BnF
assessment_reason: Contemporary 1756 sheet by a royal geographer, held by a national library, public domain, with its own graticule and hand-coloured political outlines. Directly represents the 1756 state, so no continuity bridge is needed. Positional uncertainty measured at ~3 km against an independent settlement check.

source_title: Hinton 1756, seat of war between the Prussians and Austrians — Utrecht UB
assessment_reason: Record exists and is period-correct, but the repository's rights metadata is unusable, so the file was not acquired and it cannot serve as authority. Corroboration of the Vaugondy boundaries therefore remains OUTSTANDING.

Genuine 1:200,000 regional map, far finer than the 1756 Vaugondy sheet, covering the Schwarzburg and Weimar lands. It is dated 1747, so it can never be a direct 1756 boundary authority: use for 1756 would require a TERRITORIAL_CONTINUITY assertion per subject. Georeferencing was attempted and NOT completed: the neat line is skewed in the scan and the graticule numerals could not be read unambiguously at the available resolution. No GCP was invented, so no transform exists yet.
Authority for WHICH territorial actors existed in 1756, not for where their boundaries ran. Used only for polity existence and status.
Collection-level description only; no individual archival signature was verified, so it supports the separate-administration finding but is not cited as pinpoint evidence.
